description: publish_time was stored as whatever the source sent, usually raw RFC-822 ('Wed, 28 Jan 2026 22:07:57 +0000'). ORDER BY publish_time therefore sorted alphabetically ('Feb' before 'Jan'), 'since' filtering was meaningless, and date(publish_time) returned NULL so the daily sentiment rollup matched almost nothing.
resolution: normalize.to_iso() is the single storage format: UTC, second precision, trailing Z. A migration rewrites existing rows. Rollups group on substr(publish_time,1,10) rather than date(), which is version-independent. Test asserts RFC-822 strings sort wrongly and ISO ones sort correctly.

title: Resolve one canonical Yahoo listing per instrument, ranked by exchange
rationale: The Trading212 catalogue's currency field is unreliable, so it cannot drive exchange choice: it lists TSLA as an EUR instrument. Two rules earned their keep from live failures. (1) Search by company name as well as ticker: 6RJ0 (Trading212's code for Rocket Lab) only finds its thin German line by ticker, while a name search surfaces RKLB on NASDAQ; the early-exit threshold must be 'US primary only' or it stops on XETRA. (2) Demote LSE International Board tickers, which all start with a digit: Yahoo labels 0NCA.L plain 'LSE' so it outranked XETRA, but it had 15 daily bars in a month vs 23 on IVU.DE.

description: A matching base symbol was accepted as identity during symbol resolution, so APP.AX (Appen Limited) resolved as AppLovin because 'APP.AX'.split('.')[0] == 'APP'. Tickers collide across exchanges.
resolution: Require name similarity >= 55 OR an exact symbol match; a base-symbol match alone is not enough. Verified: token_set_ratio('applovin','appen limited') is 47.6, safely below the floor. Test: tests/test_symbols.py::test_a_different_company_sharing_a_ticker_is_rejected.

description: db.news.get_news([]) returned every article in the table, because 'if short_names:' treats an empty list and None identically. The route guarded it, but an empty watchlist reaching the DB layer directly would have dumped everything.
resolution: None means 'no filter', [] means 'no results' and returns early. Test: test_no_symbols_returns_nothing_rather_than_everything.

description: 'with sqlite3.connect(...) as conn' commits or rolls back but never CLOSES the connection, so every one of ~60 data-access functions leaked a connection per call (masked by refcount collection).
resolution: One project-level @contextmanager that sets PRAGMAs, wraps 'with conn' for the transaction and closes in a finally. Nothing else constructs connections. Also: WAL writes sibling -wal/-shm files, so the Docker volume had to move from ./stocky.db to the ./data directory.

description: INSERT OR IGNORE silently swallows NOT NULL violations. The user_stocks -> watchlist migration lost follows whose legacy created_at was NULL, because watchlist.created_at is NOT NULL and OR IGNORE discarded the row without complaint.
resolution: COALESCE(MIN(created_at), strftime(...)) in the migration SELECT. Caught only by a test that built a legacy DB with NULL created_at; the real DB happened to have values, so it worked by luck.

content: Prices live in two row kinds in one table, distinguished by an 'interval' column: '1d' is an official daily close stamped at midnight UTC, 'snap' is whatever the price was at an hourly refresh.
